learn.canDo: Design uploads with presigned multipart URLs and cut storage cost with lifecycle tiers, stating what each tier gives up.
learn.why: Almost every product stores files. Knowing direct upload and tiering separates working designs from ones that melt app servers and budgets.
learn.keyIdea: Keep bytes off your servers; let old data sink.

learn.canDo: Explain term-to-document posting lists, intersect them from the shortest, and weigh positions against index size.
learn.why: Search is behind every product with a search box. The inverted index is the one idea to know.
learn.keyIdea: Do the reading once, at index time.

learn.canDo: Index points by geohash or similar cells, size cells to the search radius, and search neighbouring cells to avoid edge misses.
learn.why: Nearby search is the heart of ride-hailing and delivery designs. Cell size and edges are the follow-up questions.
learn.keyIdea: Cells about the size of the radius, plus their neighbours.

learn.canDo: Plan compression, downsampling tiers and retention for a metrics store, and keep label cardinality bounded.
learn.why: Metrics and IoT data overwhelm general databases. Tiering and cardinality are the levers that matter.
learn.keyIdea: Keep the recent past sharp and the distant past blurred.

chapter.story: Pigeon's data stops looking like rows, and the team meets stores built for files, words, places and time.
outcomes: Store and serve files cheaply with object storage
Find nearby things with cell indexes
Keep metrics affordable with compression and rollups
chapter.why: A general database can hold anything and does nothing well at scale. Each store here exploits the shape of one kind of data.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can match a data shape to its store and give the numbers. At work you will know when Postgres has stopped being the right answer.
